title: QUIC RFC 9000 Stream-Control Frame Focused Proof
purpose: Describe the focused proof boundary for RFC 9000 RESET_STREAM and STOP_SENDING frame behavior, field encoding, parser rejection, and stream-state error handling.
design_summary: The stream-control frame proof stays on existing production seams. QuicFrameCodec remains the canonical RESET_STREAM and STOP_SENDING wire-format parser/formatter. QuicConnectionStreamState remains the canonical receive/send state-machine seam for RESET_STREAM discard, final-size accounting, STOP_SENDING receipt, and STREAM_STATE_ERROR classification. QuicConnectionRuntime.Streams remains the canonical application action seam for protected RESET_STREAM and STOP_SENDING packet emission.
data_and_state_considerations: RESET_STREAM proof covers type 0x04, Stream ID, Application Protocol Error Code, Final Size, required field sequence, buffered-data discard, receive abort reason storage, final-size rejection, and send-only stream errors. STOP_SENDING proof covers type 0x05, Stream ID, Application Protocol Error Code, required field sequence, Recv and Size Known send eligibility, locally initiated uncreated stream errors, receive-only stream errors, target stream identity, and application reason forwarding.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Malformed varint fields are rejected at the frame-codec seam; packet-level close emission remains owned by packet-processing requirements.
RESET_STREAM releases buffered receive data and can therefore produce MAX_DATA credit evidence as a side effect.
STOP_SENDING is not emitted after a peer RESET_STREAM has already reset the receive side.
Maximum QUIC varint values are preserved by the field-level parser/formatter tests without broadening stream-ID runtime validity claims.
The proof records current runtime behavior for Recv and Size Known STOP_SENDING emission only; other stream-state policy remains owned by S3/S4 stream-state requirements.
alternatives_considered: Keep the broad frame-codec tests as the only S19P4/S19P5 proof; rejected because live triage requires focused requirement-home evidence.
Change production frame parsing while decomposing proof; rejected because the existing parser already satisfies the targeted wire behavior.
Fold the remaining S19 frame families into this slice; rejected to keep RESET_STREAM and STOP_SENDING closure bounded.
risks: The proof does not claim packet-level connection-close emission for every malformed stream-control frame.
S19P1 and S19P2 frame-family requirements remain outside this slice.
Public API behavior beyond the tested application abort seams remains outside this slice.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This design covers focused S19P4 and S19P5 RESET_STREAM and STOP_SENDING frame proof only: wire fields, runtime emission, receive-state discard, stream-state errors, and application reason propagation.
